capacity_gross_kwh.notes: "Upgraded 84 kWh battery" (Hyundai UK); Electrek relays 84 kWh for the US car. Treated as gross.

capacity_usable_kwh.notes: Estimated: EV Database lists 80.0 kWh usable (itself an estimate) for the 84.0 kWh European IONIQ 6 N; same 84 kWh pack.

chemistry.notes: Estimated: EV Database lists NMC cathode for the 84 kWh IONIQ 6 N (European).

nominal_voltage_class.notes: Hyundai: 800 V charging system (400/800 V multi-charging; EVDB 697 V nominal).

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: the standard IONIQ 6 (same model and platform) has the navigation-triggered battery heater (this US launch release) plus a manual Battery Conditioning Mode (CE1 manual, src-hyundai-om-ce1-2025-us); carried to the N as the same model family. Hyundai UK says the N has an upgraded coolant heater and thermal management (src-hyundai-uk-ioniq6-n-range-charging); its "preconditions the battery" line may describe the N track battery mode, which is not counted here. No N-specific manual found.
Estimated: companion to the value from src-hyundai-ww-ioniq6-la-2022 (manual control from the CE1 2025 US manual).

dc_max_kw.notes: Hyundai UK footnote: car accepts up to 240 kW in optimal conditions (page headline 350 kW is the charger). Other figures: CarExpert AU 260 kW, EV Database 263 kW. UK-spec figure, assumed same for the US car.

ac_max_kw.notes: Estimated: the US IONIQ 6 (same model) has a 10.9 kW onboard charger (US launch release); Hyundai says the N has an enhanced ICCU but gives no kW. CarExpert (Australian N) says up to 10.5 kW, EVDB 11 kW (all within 5 %). No US N figure found.

published_10_80_min.notes: About 18 min 10-80 % on a 350 kW charger (Hyundai claim relayed by Electrek).
